clue.text: House may decree self-government

parts.note: a house is a home
to decree is to rule, as a monarch rules

explanation.surface: Parliament may legislate to grant a region its own government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' looks like a chamber of Parliament, but here it simply means a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Home rule is the governing of a region or country by its own people rather than a distant power.

clue.text: Frank has two small houses

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
a nest is a small home, for birds

explanation.surface: A man named Frank owns a pair of cottages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and candid both mean truthful and open.

clue.text: Ideal pen for an examiner

parts.note: a pen named for what examiners do to scripts, which also names the examiner themselves

explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip pen has this name, and so does the person who grades exam papers.

clue.text: Row in band proves riotous

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ring is a band, as worn on a finger
an oar is used to row a boat

explanation.surface: A quarrel among musicians turns into a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but here it is the verb for propelling a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Roaring and riotous both describe loud, boisterous, unrestrained behaviour.

clue.text: Woman wrongly reviled for being craven

parts.note: Lily is a woman's name

indicators.note: the letters of reviled are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman is unfairly abused as a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily-livered is an idiom for cowardly, from the old belief that a pale liver showed fear.

clue.text: Elevate to the lords? That's a mockery!

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a peerage being handed out as a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a politician raised to the peerage is said to be sent up to the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sent up is to be promoted to a higher body such as the Lords; a parody or satire is also called this.

clue.text: Nurse put in sword as a centrepiece

indicators.note: the abbreviation for a nurse is placed inside the fencing sword

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword
RGN is Registered General Nurse, a British nursing qualification

explanation.surface: A nurse plunges a sword into a table ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: RGN is a British nursing title; 'put in' places it inside EPEE after EPE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental stand of dishes used to decorate the middle of a dining table.

clue.text: Reveal that daughter lives in the vicinity

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter, as in family trees
to live is to be, so lives gives is
close means nearby

explanation.surface: Someone tells that their daughter has moved in nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to make known or expose, the same as to reveal.

clue.text: Put off offering job to card-cutter

parts.note: a post is a position of employment
the pone is the card player, to the dealer's right, who cuts the pack

explanation.surface: A recruiter offers employment to a card player.
explanation.walkthrough: PONE is an old card-game term for the player who cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone is to defer to a later time, which is what to put off means.

clue.text: In general, no Frenchman enters motoring contest

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one piece entering another means it goes inside it

parts.note: a rally is a competitive motoring event
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: Usually a French driver does not take part in a car rally.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes after the R of RALLY, giving RMALLY after NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually and as a rule are synonyms of the phrase, describing what typically happens.

clue.text: Against sending vicar back to south America

indicators.note: sending something back turns the word for vicar around

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a title for a vicar
S is the compass abbreviation for south
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A protest against a clergyman being deported to South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending ... back' reverses REV to give VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Versus is the Latin for opposed to, as in one team playing another.

clue.text: Dish of the day is peculiar

explanation.surface: A restaurant's featured meal turns out to be odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's featured offering is called by this name; unusual or particular to something is the other sense.

clue.text: Drink urge on freak out

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
to flip is to lose one's temper or freak out

explanation.surface: A drink makes someone so excitable they lose control.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-flip is a hot beverage of beer or spirits mixed with beaten egg and sugar.

clue.text: English trial again disrupted by equal-rights supporter

indicators.note: the letters of trial and again are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A campaigner for equality halts a second English court case.
explanation.definitionFit: An egalitarian believes all people deserve the same rights and opportunities.

clue.text: Save a region in ruins, and explain why

indicators.note: something in ruins is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A plea to rescue a devastated area and justify the plea.
explanation.definitionFit: To justify an action is to offer the grounds or motive for it.

clue.text: Made supreme effort, though under stress

explanation.surface: Someone tries their hardest while feeling the pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Strained can mean exerted to the utmost, and also tense or forced.

clue.text: Retired copper allowed to be outspoken

parts.note: ex means former, so retired
P stands for a penny, a copper coin
licit means lawful or allowed

explanation.surface: A former policeman feels free to speak his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but it is a penny coin, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit means stated plainly and frankly, leaving nothing implied.

clue.text: He knows his stuff!

parts.note: the idiom for an expert is read literally: a person whose craft is stuffing animal skins

explanation.definitionFit: A taxidermist stuffs and mounts the skins of dead animals, so stuffing is literally his trade.

clue.text: Miners with mates in oz!

explanation.surface: Mining men and their Australian pals.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australian slang a digger is a comrade, originally a gold miner, later a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who excavate are one sense; Australian slang for pals or soldiers is the other.

clue.text: Sound attempt by corps to unearth old ship

indicators.note: the word for attempt is spoken, giving a spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: a try is an attempt
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers make a solid effort to dig up an ancient vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but it signals the soundalike TRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient warship with three banks of oars.

clue.text: A brother gets up on time? That's unexpected!

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A brother rises punctually, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt means sudden and without warning.

clue.text: Space traveller needs gauge containing zero indicator

indicators.note: the word for a gauge holds the zero within it

parts.note: a meter is a measuring gauge
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: An astronaut needs a dial that reads zero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts O inside METER before its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a piece of rock from space that burns up as it enters the atmosphere.

clue.text: Claimed member is involved in dodgy deal

indicators.note: one piece involved in another is wrapped up inside it
a dodgy arrangement is unsound, so the letters of deal are rearranged

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: A politician is accused of a part in a shady agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' turns DEAL into ALED; 'is involved in' puts LEG inside it after AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleged means asserted without proof, as in a supposed crime.

clue.text: A mariner in the distance appears cordial

indicators.note: the sailor's abbreviation sits inside the word for a distance

parts.note: a mile is a measure of distance
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor glimpsed far off seems friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AB inside MILE, giving MIABLE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable and cordial are synonyms meaning warm and friendly.

clue.text: He steals one quid

explanation.surface: A thief is described along with a single pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A quid is British slang for a pound sterling; so is nicker, and to nick is to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who pilfers is one sense; British slang for a pound sterling is the other.

clue.text: Make minor adjustments to magnificent melody

parts.note: fine means splendid or magnificent
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A composer tweaks a splendid tune.
explanation.definitionFit: To fine-tune is to make small precise corrections to get something exactly right.

clue.text: Silly Dorothy is hotheaded

parts.note: Dot is a pet form of the name Dorothy
taken as written

indicators.note: the head of the word hot is its first letter, attached to the end of hotheaded

explanation.surface: A woman named Dorothy is called foolish for her quick temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hotheaded' splits into 'hot' and 'headed': the head of hot is H.
explanation.definitionFit: Dottish is an old word for dotty, meaning foolish or slightly mad.

clue.text: One who besieges the stock market?

definitions.text: One who besieges the stock market?

parts.words: One who besieges the stock market?
parts.note: to invest a town is to lay siege to it, so a besieger of the markets is a person who puts money into shares

explanation.definitionFit: An investor puts capital into shares, and invest also has an old military sense of encircling a town.
